Download
Assetto Corsa import

Your AC cars and tracks, in ApexSim

If you own Assetto Corsa, the cars and circuits already on your disk convert into ApexSim in one step, from the launcher. No command line, no editing files.

Download ApexSim What converts

Four steps, once

  1. 1Open the launcher

    In the ApexSim launcher, choose Manage content > Import from Assetto Corsa.

  2. 2Pick a folder

    A car's folder or a track's from your Assetto Corsa install, or the whole cars or tracks folder to bring everything at once. The launcher tells cars and tracks apart itself.

  3. 3Let it run

    A window shows each car or layout as it converts, and a report at the end. The first time, it needs Python 3.11 or newer from python.org and sets the rest up on its own.

  4. 4Race

    Restart the game and its server: the cars are in the garage, the circuits on the globe, ready for a race, a hotlap or the AI.

What converts

Not just the model

The importers read Assetto Corsa's own physics files and map them onto ApexSim's simulation, so an imported car drives on its own figures, not a guess.

Cars

  • The body, wheels and steering wheel, seated and lit, with working lights and mirrors
  • Every skin, as a livery you can pick in the lobby
  • The cockpit's eye point, wheel and mirrors for the cockpit view
  • Mass, suspension geometry, springs, dampers, bars and bump stops
  • The engine's torque curve, its turbo boost per gear and its rev limits
  • Every tyre compound, with its grip, wear, temperature window and pressure
  • Wings and floor, with their ride-height maps and the wings that move with speed
  • Brakes, carbon or steel, hybrids and their energy, the DRS flap
  • Parts that come off in a crash, as on the shipped cars

Circuits

  • Every layout of a track folder, each one a circuit of its own
  • The road as a mesh with AC's own surfaces and their grip, kerbs and run-off
  • Walls and barriers the cars stop against
  • The racing line, sectors, grid slots and DRS zones
  • The pit lane with a box per car, where the layout has one
  • The track's textures and preview picture
  • Its real place on Earth for the famous circuits, so the sun, the air and the weather are right
Then it races

Like any other car or circuit

The whole simulation

Tyre heat and wear, damage, fuel, weather, track evolution and the pit lane all apply to an import, and the AI races it.

Online too

Everyone imports from their own copy. Two players importing the same car get the same id, and the content checksum confirms you are all racing on the same data.

Re-run any time

Importing again gives byte-identical files. A newer importer can replace an earlier import, and each import keeps a report of exactly what it read and wrote.

From a command line

Building from source? python tools/ac_car_import.py and python tools/ac_import.py take a folder, or --all for a whole collection.

What does not

The edges

  • Content encrypted by Custom Shaders Patch is refused, never decrypted.
  • Tracks without an AI line, and point-to-point stages.
  • Pit stops on a layout with no pit lane in its AI files.
  • AC's night lighting and its normal and detail maps: surfaces keep their colour textures.
  • Physics AC has no figure for (brake pads, aero from body roll, porpoising) take ApexSim's defaults.
Yours, and only yours

Your content stays on your machine

Nothing bundled

ApexSim ships converters, never Assetto Corsa's cars, tracks, textures or physics.

Nothing shared

Imports go to your own custom folders, which a release never includes and ApexSim never uploads.

Your own copy

The importers read the install you own. The first run shows a notice about personal use and mod authors' terms.

ApexSim is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Kunos Simulazioni, 505 Games or any Assetto Corsa mod author. Assetto Corsa is a trademark of its owner and is named here only to say which files the importers read. ApexSim ships no Assetto Corsa content: the importers convert content you already own, on your own machine, for your own personal use, and what they make is never shared or uploaded by ApexSim. You use them at your own risk, and it is up to you to respect the terms of the game and of every mod's author; some mod authors do not allow their work to be converted.

In active development

Get on the grid

Download the release, unzip it and run launcher.exe. It starts the game, with a local server if you want one.
